cards.explanation: The answer is that the sufferings are not comparable to the glory. Paul, an apostle writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), says it plainly: "I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us." (Romans 8:18) Not comparable. These two don't even fit on the same scale, friends. I think that's the kind of math that lets a tired person breathe a little.

The answer is the sons of God. Paul writes, "The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God." (Romans 8:19) Creation is leaning forward in its chair, friends. It's waiting on the sons of God to be revealed.

The answer is True. Paul says, "For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope" (Romans 8:20) Creation didn't choose this, friends. And notice that little word at the end: hope. The sentence doesn't stop at futility.

The answer is that it will be set free from its decay. That's the hope. Paul says "…the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God." (Romans 8:21) Free from bondage, friends, and brought into glorious freedom. Creation gets in on the good news too.

The answer is False. Paul says the whole creation "…has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time." (Romans 8:22) So as he writes, the groaning is still going. Childbirth pains, friends, and everybody knows those are leading somewhere.

The answer is the redemption of their bodies. Paul says believers "…groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies." (Romans 8:23) He doesn't leave adoption hanging. He tells you what it is, and it includes our bodies. I'll admit, my old stamper body would love that news.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?" (Romans 8:24) Hope is for what's still ahead. Once you can see it, you're not hoping anymore, you're holding it.

The word is patiently. Paul says, "But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently." (Romans 8:25) Waiting patiently for something unseen is hard, friends. I should know, I did a lot of it in a dusty drawer.

The answer is False. Paul says, "For we do not know how we ought to pray…" (Romans 8:26) He says it about "we," so he's counting himself in. Plenty of us run out of words, and that's nothing to be ashamed of.

The answer is with groans too deep for words. Paul says, "…the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words." (Romans 8:26) That's help for when we don't know how we ought to pray. Those groans go deeper than any sentence we could put together.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God." (Romans 8:27) The Spirit's praying runs along the will of God. That's good news when we don't know how we ought to pray.

The answer is True. Paul says, "And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose." (Romans 8:28) Notice who it's for: those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose. And he says all things, friends, not some things.

The answer is to be conformed to the image of His Son. Paul says, "For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son…" (Romans 8:29) The goal is to look like the Son. Not a title and not a job, friends, but the image of Jesus.

The word is brothers. Paul says it's "…so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers." (Romans 8:29) The Son isn't alone at the front of the line, friends. He's the firstborn with many brothers behind Him.

The answer is that they are glorified. That's the last link. Paul says, "those He justified, He also glorified." (Romans 8:30) Called, justified, glorified. And look at it, friends: Paul says it as one unbroken chain, and glorified is where it lands.
